payload.lessonGoal: Explain why KV cache dominates long-context serving costs and how CED plus CSA2 reduce that footprint to 890 bytes per token.
payload.learnerAssumption: Student understands basic Transformer attention but not specific cache compression techniques or HBM constraints.
payload.centralQuestion: How do architectural changes shrink the massive memory footprint of long-context models?

requiredClaims.statement: Global KV cache storage dominates runtime memory usage for sufficiently long sequences.
Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture halves prefill computation by projecting decoder KV from encoder states.
CSA2 cross-layer reuse and FP4 caching reduce global KV footprint to roughly one quarter of baseline.

requiredMechanisms.statement: Decoder global KV is projected directly from final encoder hidden states rather than computed layer-wise.
CSA2 shares main KV and indexer K across layers, allowing Reuse modes to skip generation entirely.

scenes.teachingGoal: Demonstrate how CED projection and CSA2 reuse mechanisms combine to drastically reduce global KV cache size.
scenes.learnerShouldUnderstand: The global KV cache is the bottleneck; CED reduces its generation cost while CSA2 reduces its storage size via sharing.
scenes.mentalModel: A large reservoir (KV cache) filling up as context grows, with two valves (CED, CSA2) controlling inflow and volume.

beats.purpose: Establish global KV cache as the primary memory constraint in long contexts.
beats.narrationDraft: As context length grows, the global key-value cache fills your high-bandwidth memory until it becomes the dominant bottleneck.

beats.purpose: Introduce Causal Encoder-Decoder as a mechanism to reduce KV generation cost.
beats.narrationDraft: The Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture projects decoder keys and values directly from the final encoder hidden states.

beats.purpose: Clarify how CED avoids redundant computation during prefill phase.
beats.narrationDraft: This projection allows the model to activate only half the parameters during prefill, cutting computational overhead significantly.

beats.purpose: Introduce CSA2 as the mechanism for reducing stored cache volume through layer sharing.
beats.narrationDraft: Compressed Sparse Attention 2 further shrinks storage by sharing main key-value pairs and indexers across multiple transformer layers.

beats.purpose: Explain how Reuse modes skip generation entirely to save space.
beats.narrationDraft: In Reuse mode, layers simply borrow existing keys and indices from previous layers instead of generating new ones.

beats.purpose: Add FP4 quantization as a final multiplier to reduce byte count.
beats.narrationDraft: Finally, storing these shared caches in four-bit precision halves the remaining storage requirement without losing accuracy.

beats.purpose: Summarize the combined effect on total cache footprint.
beats.narrationDraft: Together, these optimizations shrink the global cache footprint to eight hundred ninety bytes per token, roughly one quarter of before.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache reduction only affects inference speed, not memory capacity.
misconceptions.correction: Reducing KV cache size directly lowers High Bandwidth Memory requirements, enabling longer contexts on existing hardware.

misconceptions.claim: CED removes all decoder computation during prefill.
misconceptions.correction: CED still computes sliding window attention locally in the decoder, but skips global KV generation.

evidenceRefs.quote: For sufficiently long sequences, global KV therefore dominates the runtime KV footprint, which is constrained by HBM capacity.
We adopt a Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture, in which decoder global KV is projected from the final encoder hidden states.
Instead, they are projected directly from the hidden state of the (L/2)-th layer... using layer-dependent projection weights.
This design enables the model to activate 16B parameters per token during decode but only 8B parameters during prefill.
CSA2 applies cross-layer reuse to global KV (including main KV and indexer K) and Top-K indices to substantially reduce KV cache storage.
Reuse Mode reuses both global KV and the Top-K indices in a preceding layer, and directly performs sparse attention.
Compared with the FP8 main KV cache in DeepSeek-V4, this format nearly halves the storage footprint, both in HBM and when offloaded to SSD.
These designs reduce its global KV cache footprint (always in HBM) to 890 bytes per token, roughly 1/4 of the corresponding footprint of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
